name: Tempester n°63, 1.6.9.0 form (n°65): the five Release parameters capped at 123 only while a Voice chip does not run Tempester Voice; 127 when the six chips answered a Tempester Voice word 0x16-0x79 (1.6.7.0 and 1.6.8.0 keep patch/release_cap_1670.json, exact 0x16; 1.6.6.0 and older patch/release_cap.json)
explanation: 1.6.7.0's form (patch/release_cap_1670.json) with one change, the start-up test VOICE_CHECK, at the same place and in the same 16 words (14 used, the 2 after its tail jump left erased): every other routine keeps its address and its words. Why: 1.6.7.0 lifted the cap only when the six chips answered exactly 0x16 (Tempester Voice 1.5.1.0 and 1.5.1.1); each Tempester Voice OS now has a word of its own (1.5.1.2: 0x17, patch/voice/version_reply_1512.json), and every one from 1.5.1.0 on has the finite release 101-127 in the five envelopes (patch/voice/release_curve.json). Rule: a chip runs Tempester Voice when its 0xFE00 halfword w is 0x16 <= w <= 0x79 (unsigned: w - 0x16 < 0x64). Lower bound: DSI's 1.5 answers 0x15, its older Voice OSes lower words; a chip that did not answer gives 0x0000 or 0xFFFF. Upper bound: main's start-up loop takes 1-0x79 as a reply, and the System screen shows (w & 0x7F) >> 4 . w & 0xF, so 0x79 is the last word a Voice OS can be shown as; the whole halfword is compared (0x0116, 0x8016 refused). VOICE_CHECK (hook [address], right after the sixth read; the replaced [routine](0xF500, 0) made as a tail jump) loops over the halfwords [address] and writes RELEASE_LIFT [address] = 4 when the six are in range, else 0. The gates (CAP_WORD, CAP_BURST, CAP_LOAD) and the lifted readers (MAX_KNOB, MAX_DISPLAY, MAX_NRPN) are 1.6.7.0's, unchanged. Code 0x9d07be00-0x9d07be37 and 0x9d07be40-0x9d07bfaf; RAM [address] (one byte). Proof: tools/sim_release_cap.py --lift --range and its counter-proofs (the exact 0x16 test of 1.6.8.0 against six 0x17 chips, a range that takes 0x15 or 0x7A). Source: release_cap_1690.s.
